# CP-12-27: 3.x code numbers in CONFUSIONS and DEVIATIONS, generated by script from the crosswalk

**In plain words.** The tie-breaker file (CONFUSIONS.md) and the deviations log (DEVIATIONS.md)
still describe several 3.x matters with the old 2.x code numbers, such as "4.2.2" for what is now
Emotion Regulation & Coping (Y4.2). A reader of the 3.x codebook cannot follow them. The house
rule is that code numbers are never changed by hand: a script applies the published old-to-new map
(the 2.5.1-to-3.0.0 crosswalk) and a test checks the result. This change adds that script and
test. In the deviations log it adds the new number beside each old one. For four tie-breakers
(coping vs symptoms, family codes, CASEL skills with no code of their own, and trauma) it writes a
3.x copy in a new 3.x section, leaving the 2.x originals in place because the retired 2.x codebook
still uses them. The family tie-breaker's copy is marked open: it contradicts the live Family
Participation & Leadership (F1.9) and Family Engagement Systems (A2.6) codes, and it waits for you
to re-review the "family advisory board" row (S176). Nothing the coding model reads changes.

## Problem

1. **CONFUSIONS.md has no 3.x ids at all.** It is the 2.x registry ("Code numbers follow v2.0.0").
   Four entries matter to 3.x and are pointed at from 3.x material: CF-003 (rule 6 restates it),
   CF-008 (rule 10), CF-016 (rule 14, and the `casel-2020` registry note says "see CONFUSIONS.md
   CF-016"), CF-019 (rule 18 proposed in CP-12-19). Batch 1 item 16, batch 3 later item 9.
2. **DEVIATIONS.md's 3.x entries use bare 2.x numbers** for the codes they merged or carried, e.g.
   FD-P02 "one code for 2.4.0's 4.2.1 and 4.2.2". 24 lines in FD-P02..FD-P20.
3. **The 2.x entries cannot simply be rewritten in place.** `sync.test.ts` checks every CF entry
   against the retired but registered `codebooks/original.ts` (S3.2): each **Codes:** line must name
   live 2.x codes, and each pair a 2.x hint separates must be covered by an entry. Its code pattern
   also reads "Y4.2" as the 2.x code "4.2". Rewriting CF-003 in place would break both checks, and
   adding to `PAIRS_WITHOUT_CF` is not allowed. So 3.x copies are generated into a separate section,
   and the tests read each section with its own codebook.
4. **CF-008 contradicts the live 3.x codes (batch 3 later item 9; G14).** Its rule sends Epstein
   Type 3 volunteering to the family-program relationship code and Types 5 and 6 to the
   organization's systems; live F1.9 cites Types 3 and 5 and A2.6 cites Types 3 and 6. Its gold row
   G-021 ("The program will create a family advisory board with parent representatives.") is the
   same text as S176, which Severin adjudicated F1.9, not the A2.6 that CF-008's rule gives.

## Change

### Script: `codebook-refinement/v3/renumber_2x_refs.py`

Same pattern as `renumbering/renumber_v2_0_0.py`: derive the map, apply it only where named,
print every changed line, refuse to run twice.

- **Map.** Read `v3/crosswalk-2.5.1-to-3.0.0.csv`; key = the 2.x code at the start of `old_code`.
  `one-to-one` and `merge` rows map to `new_code`. `split` rows (1.3, 1.6, 6.1, 6.4, 8.1, 9.1, 11.3)
  have no single target: the script never picks one. A 2.x domain reference ("Domain 12") maps to a
  3.x domain only if every code in it goes to one 3.x domain; Domain 12 goes to F1 and F2, so it is
  flagged.
- **Token pattern.** `(?<![\w.#§$-])(\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}(?:\.\d)?)(?![.\d]\d|\.x)`, and only tokens
  that are crosswalk keys are touched. So "S4.9", "2.4.0", "3.0 proposal", "PR #33" and
  "current-inventory.md 4.3" are left alone (none is a key, or the look-behind excludes it).
- **DEVIATIONS.md**, only between "## Codebook 3.x" and "## Drift count": each key token becomes
  "<old> (now <new>)", or "<old> (now <new> and <targets>)" for a split. A token already followed
  by " (now " is skipped, so the script is safe to re-run after per-domain CPs edit an entry.
  FD-001..FD-005 (the 2.x section) are not touched: they describe `codebooks/original.ts`.
- **CONFUSIONS.md.** For each id in `SOURCES = {'CF-003': 'CF-031', 'CF-008': 'CF-unassigned (3.x copy of CF-008)',
  'CF-016': 'CF-032', 'CF-019': 'CF-033'}`, copy the 2.x block into the 3.x section, replace each
  one-to-one or merge token with its 3.x code, write a split or multi-domain token as
  "<old> [2.x; split in 3.0: …]", map each **Gold:** G-id to the v3 design row with the same
  `outcome_text` (exact match, from `gold/original.gold.csv` to `gold/youth_outcomes_v3.gold.csv`),
  and check that the v3 row's adjudicated code is the code the entry routes it to. Any split,
  multi-domain or gold mismatch sets the entry's status to "open" and is printed. The 2.x block is
  left exactly as it is.
- **Override (one row).** `OVERRIDE = {('CF-016', '6.4'): ('Y5.6', 'rulesText rule 14: "initiative or personal agency -> Y5.6 (Y6.4 if civic)"')}`.
  The crosswalk sends 6.4 to Y5.5 with Y5.4 as re-review target, but the live 3.x rule already
  routes this CASEL skill to Y5.6 (Search Institute "Personal power", registry support for Y5.6).
  The override copies the live rule's code; the test checks it against rulesText.
- Flags: `--dry-run` (default; prints) and `--write`.

### Tests (same branch)

1. `sync.test.ts` and `registry.test.ts` read only the part of `CONFUSIONS.md` before
   "## Codebook 3.x tie-breakers" (CP-12-15's design; whichever of CP-12-15, CP-12-27, CP-12-31
   lands first makes this edit, the others drop it). This keeps the 2.x checks exactly as they are
   and stops "Y4.2" being read as 2.x "4.2".
2. `codebooks/youthOutcomesV3.test.ts`, in `describe('crosswalk 2.5.1 -> 3.0.0 ...')`:
   - **generated CF entries match the crosswalk.** For each `### CF-P..` block with a
     "_Renumbered from CF-xxx_" line, map the 2.x block's **Codes:** tokens through the crosswalk
     (one-to-one and merge only; splits and multi-domain tokens must appear as "[2.x; …]"), apply
     `OVERRIDE`, and expect the 3.x block's **Codes:** line to equal the result. Expect each
     **Gold:** id to be an adjudicated design row whose `outcome_text` equals the 2.x G-row's,
     and, unless the entry is "open", whose `v3_gold` is one of the entry's codes.
   - **the override agrees with rulesText.** `rulesText` contains "initiative or personal agency -> Y5.6".
   - **DEVIATIONS 3.x numbers are annotated.** In the 3.x section, every crosswalk-key token is
     followed by " (now ".
3. The 3.x CF check CP-12-15 drafts (≥2 adjudicated rows per code) applies to new tie-breakers.
   Generated entries carry the 2.x rule instead (S3.1, as `registry.test.ts` applies it: at least
   two adjudicated rows per entry); CF-031, CF-032 and CF-033 have 3, 2 and 2. Open entries (CF-unassigned (3.x copy of CF-008))
   are exempt, like "proposed" ones.
